dimensions.assessment: Affects intelligence agencies, foreign intelligence targets, and U.S. persons whose communications may be incidentally acquired during the extension period.
dimensions.evidence: Information about U.S. persons may incidentally be acquired by this type of surveillance and subsequently queried

dimensions.assessment: Maintains the status quo by extending existing surveillance authorities for a brief, limited duration without altering their legal scope.
dimensions.evidence: This act extends the authorities of Title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) until June 12, 2026.

dimensions.assessment: No changes to federal spending or revenue are stated or implied beyond the continued operation of existing intelligence programs.
Amends the FISA Amendments Act of 2008 solely by altering expiration dates.
dimensions.evidence: Section 403(b) of the FISA Amendments Act of 2008... is amended... by striking April 30, 2026 and inserting June 12, 2026

dimensions.assessment: Provides a temporary extension of authorities lasting approximately six weeks, until June 12, 2026.

missing_information: Specific operational changes or procedural updates occurring during the extension period
importance_detail.rationale: The bill provides a short, temporary extension of existing Title VII Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act authorities from April 30, 2026, to June 12, 2026.

card.summary: H.R. 8035 extends the expiration date for Title VII of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 to October 20, 2027. It also extends transition procedures that keep existing surveillance orders, authorizations, and directives in effect until their individual expiration dates if Title VII authorities ever expire.
